name: sortstr
algorithm: Each standard library's unstable sort of n strings of 16 bytes (plan/06-m6.md 4.1, the sort row's strings): per round r each key is the 16 lowercase hex digits of splitmix64 from seed + r * 0x5555555555555555, the keys views of one buffer, sorted by byte order; every 1,024th key read back as a number times its index, plus the last, is added to the checksum with wrapping, so the checksums are the sort row's (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own algorithm; the sorted order of distinct keys is unique, so the sampled checksum checks every column sorted
notes: Algorithms: Mk Slice.Sort over str (16 bytes, so ipnsort's Lomuto partition unless the pivot sample reads increasing, std/core/core_sort.mk, D8-32, SD8-R1), str's byte order inlined as the comparator; Rust slice::sort_unstable over &str is ipnsort; Zig std.mem.sortUnstable with std.mem.lessThan is pdqsort; Go slices.Sort over string is pdqsort; C qsort over char * with strcmp is the C runtime's (UCRT on Windows), with an indirect comparison call per compare.
Every column builds its keys in one buffer and sorts views of it (Mk str, Rust &str, Zig []const u8, Go substrings of one string, C pointers to NUL-terminated keys), so no column allocates per key.
Added for SD8-R6: plan/06-m6.md section 4.1 asks for std sort of u64 and of strings; the sort row is u64 only. Publish size the contract's 10 M, one round, as the sort row's (SD8-X-10).
